newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain heightens flood fears in Manitoba.
newsitem.headline: Rain heightens flood fears in Manitoba.

text.p: Rain fell on flood-stricken southern Manitoba on Friday, raising fears that the western Canadian province's worst flooding in 145 years could become even more devastating.

More than half an inch (1.2 cm) of rain was expected to fall by Saturday in the Red River valley that includes Winnipeg, the biggest city in the province. At least 300 square miles (777 sq km) of southern Manitoba was already under water and more than 800 square miles (2,000 sq km) could be inundated by the time the Red River crests, emergency officials said.
Two boys and a man were presumed drowned so far this week in Manitoba and 66 highways in the region were closed.

The Red was expected to crest at Emerson, Manitoba, on the Canada-U.S. border on Monday, but will not crest at St. Adolphe, just south of Winnipeg, until May 5, Manitoba flood engineer engineer Larry Whitney said.
Authorities said dikes around three abandoned Red River valley towns could be washed over if floods reach the top end of projections, and the new rain raised fears for the worst.

"The numbers tell you the dikes are not high enough for the worst-case scenario in the communities of St. Adolphe, Letellier and Emerson," Canadian Armed Forces Capt. Ben Desautels said. "We fear water entering into those towns."
Don Stewart, who was sandbagging a farmer's home just north of the border, said, "It was an eerie feeling out there. I was there in 1979 and it was already higher than that."
Red River floods in 1979 covered 400 square miles (1,000 sq km) of southern Manitoba and a comparable flood in 1950 forced the evacuation of 100,000 people from Winnipeg.

"It's the worst I've seen since 1950 but things are different with the Floodway," south Winnipeg resident Barry Jones said. The Red River Floodway, a dike built in 1968 to protect Winnipeg's 650,000 residents from flooding, was raised 4.5 feet (1.5 metres) to divert the flood waters.

The Red River rose 1.7 feet (0.5 metres) on Thursday and water exceeded the previous record of the century in Emerson and Letellier by 7 p.m. EDT on Friday. Police and soldiers will go door-to-door to ensure everyone is evacuated if necessary, Manitoba's Emergency Management Organisation said.
More than 17,000 residents of the Red River valley between the U.S. border and Winnipeg were ordered from their homes by 9 p.m. EDT on Friday.

At its peak the Red River should flow at 138,000 cubic feet (3,908 cu metres) a second at Winnipeg on May 5, barring any more significant rainfall, Whitney said. The only higher levels were recorded in 1852 at 165,000 cubic feet a second (4,672 cu metres) and 1826 at 225,000 cubic feet a second (6,371 cu metres), he said.
